stem: A long-term transplant survivor asks which anatomic sites are most associated with squamous cell carcinoma. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Sun-exposed areas of skin are the predominant location
Squamous cell carcinoma occurs only on soles of the feet never exposed to light
Only mucosal surfaces inside the mouth are ever affected
Skin cancer in transplant recipients is limited to covered abdominal skin only

explanation.rationale_correct: Sun-exposed areas of skin are the predominant location of squamous cell carcinomas in transplant recipients, supporting sun-protection counseling.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sun-exposed rather than strictly non-exposed sites are described as predominant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Cutaneous sun-exposed sites are emphasized rather than oral mucosa alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sun-exposed areas are cited as predominant rather than covered abdominal skin exclusively.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Skin care → Risk of skin cancer
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Sun exposed areas of skin are the predominant location of squamous cell carcinomas

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Skin care (sun-exposed areas predominant for squamous cell carcinoma); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sun-exposed-site counseling angle paired with education combo (cctc-1105); distinct from skin-cancer incidence item (cctc-3054); anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.

stem: Which self-care practice for skin cancer surveillance aligns with standard post-transplant health-maintenance references?

options.text: Routine self-examination with immediate reporting of any changes
Avoid all skin examination because changes are never significant
Self-examination only once every 10 years regardless of findings
Report skin changes only if they occur before transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin care teaching includes routine self-examination with immediate reporting of any changes, along with annual examination by a health care provider.

rationale_incorrect.B: Routine self-examination is recommended because skin cancer risk is elevated after transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Self-examination is ongoing rather than once per decade.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant skin surveillance continues after transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Skin care
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Routine self-examination; report any changes immediately

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Skin care (routine self-exam and report changes immediately); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Skin self-examination surveillance angle distinct from annual provider exam emphasis (cctc-3103); anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.

stem: When coordinating long-term follow-up for a transplant recipient, how often should skin examination by a health care provider occur per standard references?

options.text: Only once before transplant with no further skin exams
Skin examination is discouraged after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Skin care includes examination by a health care provider annually, along with routine self-examination and sun precautions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Annual provider skin examination continues after transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Annual rather than decennial examination is recommended.
rationale_incorrect.D: Skin examination is part of long-term health maintenance rather than being discouraged.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Skin care
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Examination by a health care provider annually

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Skin care (annual provider skin examination); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Annual provider skin-exam coordination angle paired with self-examination item (cctc-3102); anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant dental health teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Regular visits to the dentist are recommended for transplant recipients.
Recipients should inform the dentist of immunosuppressed status.
Dental antibiotic prophylaxis may be required depending on the type of dental procedure.
Recipients should never discuss dental procedures with the transplant team.

explanation.rationale_correct: Regular dental visits, informing the dentist of immunosuppressed status, and possible procedure-specific prophylaxis are recommended; the transplant team should be consulted at least a week before dental appointments, so statement IV is false.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—prophylaxis may be required depending on the procedure.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because transplant-team consultation is advised before dental procedures.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → health maintenance → Dental care
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Regular visits to the dentist … Inform dentist of immunosuppressed status … Dental prophylaxis may be required … Discuss with transplant team at least a week before appointment

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → health maintenance → Dental care (regular visits, inform dentist, prophylaxis, team consult); PDF p. 118 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Post-transplant dental-care combo paired with pretransplant dental coordination (cctc-2103); anchor verified on Cupples p. 118.
